# Direct-speech fixture sources

Every clip under `services/voice/tests/fixtures/direct-speech/` is either derived from
one of the public datasets below or generated by
`services/voice/scripts/direct-speech-fixtures.py`. No private recording and no
NC- or ND-licensed material is part of the corpus.

## Common Voice 17.0, Spanish test split — CC0-1.0

- Dataset: `fsicoli/common_voice_17_0` on Hugging Face, split `audio/es/test`,
  shard `es_test_0.tar`.
- Upstream: Mozilla Common Voice 17.0, <https://commonvoice.mozilla.org/datasets>.
- Retrieval URL: <https://huggingface.co/datasets/fsicoli/common_voice_17_0/tree/8262c16bf297c87a9cd88c51997c4758ed7a8ba2/audio/es/test>
  (shard `es_test_0.tar`, revision pinned in the build script).
- Licence: CC0 1.0 Universal (public domain dedication),
  <https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/>. No attribution is required;
  crediting Mozilla Common Voice is a courtesy.
- The speakers are anonymous volunteers of the dataset. The manifest records a
  12-character prefix of the dataset's own anonymous `client_id`, never any other
  identifier.

## Mini LibriSpeech (`dev-clean-2`, OpenSLR resource 31) — CC-BY-4.0

- Retrieval URL: <https://www.openslr.org/resources/31/dev-clean-2.tar.gz>.
- Archive sha256: `176ec501490eced2d6c1f89f4f0ddc7dfe799e649e5322f8ba49fe3ff50c8012`.
- Derived from LibriSpeech: V. Panayotov, G. Chen, D. Povey, S. Khudanpur,
  "LibriSpeech: an ASR corpus based on public domain audio books", ICASSP 2015.
- Licence: CC BY 4.0, <https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/>.
- Attribution: the citation above, the OpenSLR resource page, and the speaker ids
  recorded per clip in `manifest.json`.
- Modifications, per class (the exact chain, and the level it reached, is in each
  clip's `processing` field): every LibriSpeech clip is converted to 16-bit mono
  PCM and level-normalised; `holder-direct` and `other-direct` are trimmed
  windows; `side-talk` clips are concatenations of three utterances taken from
  two speakers, with silence written into the turn gaps; `background-tv` clips
  are the same speech attenuated by 14-20 dB, low-passed at 2.8 kHz, given a short
  echo, and mixed with a generated music bed at -44 dBFS RMS and generated pink
  noise at -55 dBFS RMS. The voices are otherwise unaltered — no pitch, speed or
  content change.

## Synthetic material

`background-noise` is generated outright by the build script with `ffmpeg`
(`anoisesrc`, `sine`, `amix`, `tremolo`); the music bed and the noise floor mixed
into `background-tv` are generated the same way. No third-party material is
involved and the manifest records `license: "synthetic"` for these files.
